text:
sarah.k: Heads up — legal asked for a proposal on per-tenant sensitivity filtering + rotation for SIEM exports. We need a short plan covering classification, RBAC for incident access, and KMS/keywrap options. Looping in @matt.d and @olivia_c :eyes:

matt.d: Quick q — when you say "sensitivity" do you mean PII/auth events/stack traces? need concrete categories to set retention windows.

olivia_c: I would split into: PII (email/ssn), Auth (login/failures/token ops), Telemetry (traces/metrics) and Debug (full stack). Then: classify at ingest, store redacted view for long-term, allow raw access via JIT unwrap. :shield:

sec-bot: FYI runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/siem-exports-filtering (last updated 2026-02-14) — contains current export ACLs and JIT flow.

matt.d: For JIT unwrap we should use short-lived KMS decrypt tokens + approval ticket. Proposed flow: engineer requests access -> ticket created in ops queue -> approver (security) clicks approve -> system issues ephemeral unwrap token (30m) and logs action. Sample approval POST below: ```bash
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/unwrap-request -d '{"tenant":"T123","reason":"incident triage","duration":30}' 
```

olivia_c: On retention windows: baseline masked exports = 90d, masked raw indexes = 180d, raw snapshots only for legal/forensics holds (up to 365d) with documented justification. Also suggest per-tenant sensitivity flags so customers with higher compliance needs can opt for stricter retention or per-tenant CMK.

sarah.k: Good. What RBAC changes do we need so oncall can access raw rows during incidents but not otherwise? do we rely on existing oncall role + a separate "unwrap" entitlement?

matt.d: Proposal: keep oncall role read-only for masked views. Add a separate "raw-unmask-requester" entitlement that requires approval. Map unwrap to a service account that only exists while the ticket is open. Add audit hooks to send any unwrap event to SIEM/forensics topic.

olivia_c: One more thing — KMS options: per-tenant CMK gives best isolation but operational cost is higher. Alternative is a tenant-wrapped data key (DEK) encrypted by a global CMK with per-tenant metadata; unwrap still requires entitlement check. Recommend DEK+global CMK as compromise.

sarah.k: What about exporting to partners? need a gating policy: partners only get pre-filtered, PII-masked streams. Any raw partner exports must go through legal + contract.

matt.d: Agreed. I'll spin up an RFC with the flow diagram and the ticket API spec. Will also add tests for audit logging (must contain requester, approver, tenant, reason, duration, DEK id).

sec-bot: Incident handling checklist updated: added "verify unwrap ticket exists" step.

matt.d: I'll open the RFC PR this afternoon and ping infra for limits on snapshot sizes / retention buckets. Link will be posted here. :thumbsup:
